{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"5f5add93a721d4809b1991c117d901b9c4042992d6b170ca7f5e5835d3a50942","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:28","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: school bus distances and penalties, patrol and pedestrian violations, emergency and service vehicles, careless versus reckless driving, traffic stop conduct, fleeing penalties, pedestrians and bicyclists","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: school bus distances and penalties, patrol and pedestrian violations, emergency and service vehicles, careless versus reckless driving, traffic stop conduct, fleeing penalties, pedestrians and bicyclists
Confusable pairs from the sharing the road pages, followed by continuation facts on traffic stops, pedestrians and bicyclists; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
A school bus warns that it is about to stop with yellow and red lights that flash in turn, and the yellow lights come on 100 feet ahead of the stop in zones of 35 mph or less but 300 feet ahead in faster zones. [A01]
Why it matters: group school bus; confusable slow-zone versus fast-zone warning distance; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
A steady red signal means stop and wait for green, while a flashing red light means stop and then go when clear, just as at a stop sign. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable steady red versus flashing red; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A02
Without a divider, the duty to stop for a bus with flashing red lights covers traffic from both directions, behind the bus and facing it; only a divided roadway frees drivers on the far side. [A02]
Why it matters: group school bus; confusable undivided versus divided roads; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A02
An officer with probable cause to believe you illegally passed a stopped school bus may arrest you within four hours of the violation. [A02]
Why it matters: group school bus penalties; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A03
A driver who passes a stopped school bus faces a misdemeanor, while the vehicle's owner or lessee faces a petty misdemeanor unless they show someone else was driving. [A03]
Why it matters: group school bus penalties; confusable driver versus owner liability; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
When you sign a driver's license application, you certify that you understand the duty to stop for a school bus and know the penalties for breaking that law. [A03]
Why it matters: group school bus; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A03
Right-of-way and yielding laws rest on courtesy and common sense, and breaking them is a leading cause of traffic crashes. [A03]
Why it matters: group right-of-way; prereq for the yielding list.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A03
Coming out of a private road or driveway onto a public road, you stop and yield to pedestrians and traffic, and at intersections and crosswalks, marked or unmarked, you always yield to crossing pedestrians. [A03]
Why it matters: group right-of-way; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A04
An officer with probable cause to believe you failed to yield to an emergency vehicle may arrest you within four hours of the violation. [A04]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable with the school bus arrest window.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A04
The Move Over rule also applies to stalled or disabled vehicles and to stopped service patrol, road maintenance, utility, construction, postal, and solid waste or recycling vehicles with warning lights on. [A04]
Why it matters: group Move Over; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A04
Never drive over an unprotected fire hose unless a law enforcement officer or fire department official tells you to. [A04]
Why it matters: group fire vehicles; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A04
Keep enough distance behind the vehicle ahead to stop or turn away from a collision, adjust it for weather, traffic and road conditions, and use the three-second rule taught later in the manual. [A04]
Why it matters: group following distance; links to the driving conditions chapter.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A04
A charge of either careless or reckless driving is tried in court as a misdemeanor. [A04]
Why it matters: group careless versus reckless; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A05
On a multi-lane road, if you are nearer the left shoulder and it has room for a full lane, you may pull over onto the left shoulder instead of the right. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; confusable right versus left shoulder.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A05
If your license or insurance proof is out of reach, tell the officer where it is before reaching, and do not get out of the vehicle or approach the officer unless you ask and are given permission. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A05
If you disagree with a citation, do not argue at the roadside; explain your view in court, and ask any questions before the officer finishes the stop. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A05
Not obeying a lawful order or direction from an officer is illegal and can lead to arrest, and you should not resist if taken into custody. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A05
Traffic enforcement aims to change unsafe behavior, reduce crashes and injuries and save lives, and a warning or citation is meant to deter future unsafe driving. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A06
During a stop the officer will usually greet you, say they are a law enforcement officer, ask for your license and insurance proof, explain the reason for the stop and check that your license is valid. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A06
Identification accepted at a traffic stop includes a Minnesota or out-of-state driver's license, a temporary license, a learner's permit, a military ID, and a consulate or international driver's license. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A06
Citations go to a local jurisdiction for a hearing, and the court may offer a diversion program such as driver education training. [A06]
Why it matters: group citations; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A06
Concerns about an officer's conduct go to the officer's agency or supervisor, using the officer information printed on the citation. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R23 | anchor: A06
If someone dies because a driver fled police, the penalty reaches up to 10 years in prison and a $20,000 fine; great bodily harm brings up to seven years and $14,000; substantial bodily harm brings up to five years and $10,000. [A06]
Why it matters: group fleeing penalties; confusable harm levels; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R24 | anchor: A07
Breaking pedestrian right-of-way laws is a misdemeanor, and a second violation within a year becomes a gross misdemeanor. [A07]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; confusable with the school patrol penalty.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R25 | anchor: A07
Watch extra carefully for pedestrians on streets lined with parked cars, in poor visibility and wherever children are around, and never stop with your vehicle blocking a crosswalk. [A07]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R26 | anchor: A07
Pedestrians should obey signals, wait a few feet back from the road for the WALK signal, still yield to vehicles already in the intersection, and make eye contact so drivers yield before they cross. [A07]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R27 | anchor: A07
Where there is no crosswalk a pedestrian yields to all vehicles, and if walking on the road is necessary, walks on the left side facing oncoming traffic. [A07]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; confusable walker facing traffic versus bicyclist riding with traffic; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R28 | anchor: A07
At night or in poor visibility, pedestrians should wear light-colored clothing with reflective material or carry a flashlight, and expect that sun glare may keep drivers from seeing them. [A07]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R29 | anchor: A08
Before turning across a bicycle lane, make sure it is clear, signal, and move into the bicycle lane before you make the turn. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycle lanes; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R30 | anchor: A08
Electric-assist bicycles follow the same road rules as bicycles, while mopeds, which have a gas engine, follow different rules. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycles; confusable e-bike versus moped; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R31 | anchor: A08
Bicyclists ride just to the right of faster traffic but may move toward the center of the lane for hazards, when passing or when turning left. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R32 | anchor: A08
A bicyclist signals a right turn with the left arm bent upward or the right arm held straight out, and signals stopping with the left arm bent down toward the ground. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycle signals; confusable right turn versus stop signal; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R33 | anchor: A08
Two bicyclists may ride side by side if they stay within one lane and do not impede traffic, and riders should wear helmets for safety. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R34 | anchor: A08
At night a bicycle needs legal lights and reflectors and may use a white flashing front lamp, a red flashing rear lamp or both, and tires with spikes are allowed for traction. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R35 | anchor: A08
On sidewalks and crosswalks a bicyclist yields to pedestrians, gives an audible signal before passing them, has a pedestrian's rights and duties, and may not ride on business district sidewalks unless local authorities allow it. [A08]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]
